title: Allocator shadow-chain debugging for KV prefetch residue
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Observed gradual resident memory growth (RSS drift) on long-lived continuous-batching workloads when KV cache prefetching is enabled. Growth appears correlated with sustained mixed sequence lengths and high concurrency. Unlike prior slab/residency bugs, this case shows a stable set of small "shadow" allocations that never get reclaimed and are not visible in aggregate allocator counters. Suspect interaction between staging/pinned pool reuse and per-stream epoch bookkeeping causing allocation chain references to persist across batch boundaries.
reproduction_steps: Deploy benchmark harness 'cont-batch-kv-prefetch' (internal: drive.redwood/bench/cont-batch-kv-prefetch) against dedicated GPU pool (A100-80GB) with 128 concurrent sessions
Enable KV cache prefetch with prefetch_window=4 and pooling_mode=multi-slab
Feed mixed-length sequences (8/512/2048 tokens) following production distribution for 48+ hours
Measure RSS, CUDA resident pages, and allocator counters every 10 minutes via /metrics and nvprof traces
Collect per-stream allocation traces using the allocation-harness (internal script) and host pinned staging logs
observed_behavior: RSS increases ~2-6MB per hour until plateau or OOM
cudaMallocAsync counters show matching frees but resident pages remain allocated
Small allocation footprints (~64B-8KB) persist on the device but are not attributed to active KV entries
Host pinned staging shows repeated allocate/free cycles with allocation IDs re-used but not released to OS
Batch boundary epochs show mismatched stream epochs in trace logs (stream_epoch mismatch warnings)
Fallback to single-batch mode removes the growth
investigation_findings: Allocation traces show 'shadow chain' of device allocations referenced by transient stream metadata structures that survive eviction path
Staging pool deferred-free queue length correlates with RSS drift spikes under mixed batch sizes
Prefetch path can attach device pointers to stream-scoped metadata without proper detach on stream epoch rollover
cudamallocasync returns memory to pool but stream-quarantine path expects an explicit stream-sweep event not always emitted under continuous batching
A kernel selection optimization introduced in runtime-1.20 changes stream synchronization ordering which exposes race where epoch-callbacks can race with allocator deflate path
hypothesis: Prefetch attaches small device buffers to per-stream metadata; when batch boundaries roll streams into new epochs the detach callback is missed due to reordered kernel submission, leaving allocations referenced from a shadow linked list
The allocator pool reuses addresses and reports frees but the shadow reference prevents underlying pages from migrating out of the resident set
Pinned host staging thrashes because deferred-free is queued but never drained for these shadow allocations
proposed_actions: Add end-of-epoch allocation audit: record allocation ref counts and verify detach callbacks during stream rollover (instrumentation change)
Add a stream-quarantine drain trigger on prefetch eviction to force-check orphaned refs
Temporarily disable the kernel submission reorder optimization in runtime-1.20 branch and validate memory behavior
Add unit/integration reproducer that accelerates epoch rollover to make bug deterministic (target 1K epochs/minute)
Create follow-up runtime patch to add weak references for prefetch-attached buffers and stronger assertion on detach path
Run 72-hour soak with workload variant and collect nvprof + host pinned staging flamegraphs
short_term_mitigation: Default KV prefetch window to 2 for Dedicated clusters while investigation is ongoing
Add guard in prefetch path to fall back to synchronous detach when stream_epoch mismatch detected
Monitor affected customer Dedicated pools and notify via internal incident dashboard
long_term_fix_candidates: Redesign prefetch bookkeeping so device pointers are owned by KV cache controller not by transient stream metadata
Introduce explicit lifecycle tokens for allocations tied to epoch; on epoch commit, perform deterministic sweep
Rework allocator deferred-free drain policy so orphaned allocations are eventually reclaimed even when stream callbacks are skipped
